title: Can the ray OA also be named OB or AO?
description: A ray starts at O and passes through A, and B also lies on it. Each new name is tested by asking where the ray with that name starts. A last check reads the first letter of each name against the starting point of the drawn ray.
teaching_notes: One idea: the first letter of a ray's name is its starting point, and any other point on the ray can follow. Watch for students who think that two names with the same letters always mean the same ray.

source: Here is a ray OA. It starts at O and passes through the point A. It also passes through the point B. Can you also name it as OB? Why? Can we write OA as AO? Why or why not?
video_script.why: The child tests each name by asking where the ray with that name starts, and sees that OB names the same ray but AO does not.
video_script.substitution: Place a finger on the first letter of the name and walk along the ray.
video_script.anchor: a ray drawn from a dot at O through the points A and B, with an arrowhead at the far side
video_script.payoff_line: O B is the same ray, but eigh O is a different ray

final_answer.value: a) Yes, OB names the same ray, because it starts at O and B lies on it. b) No, AO would start at A, so it is a different ray
final_answer.spoken: yes, O B names the same ray, because it starts at O and B lies on it. No, eigh O would start at eigh, so it is a different ray

never_show: whether AO is the same ray, before the answer beat
maths_rules: A ray is named with its starting point first, followed by any other point on the ray.
The ray starts at O and passes through A and B, so B lies on it.
OB starts at O and goes through B, the same way as the ray, so OB names the same ray.
AO starts at A and goes towards O, the opposite way, so it is a different ray.
Check: the first letter of the name must be the starting point.
video_script.design: One idea: read the first letter to find where a ray starts. The ray with its dot at O stays on the board and a second ray from A is tried against it. The method is the same way as the example in the book on the ray.
